cases.expected: Empty string (no records) – toString() should return the same result as toMasterFile() for an empty zone, which is an empty string.
cases.description: Verify that a newly created Zone with no records returns an empty master file representation.

cases.expected: String containing the A record for "www.example.com." and nothing else – toString() should return the master‑file representation of a zone that only holds that record.
cases.description: Create a Zone with origin "example.com.", add a single A record (www.example.com. 3600 IN A 192.0.2.1) and verify that toString() produces a non‑empty string that includes the record line and no other records.

cases.expected: String containing the SOA, NS, A and MX records in master‑file order – toString() must list all added records correctly.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add an SOA record, an NS record, an A record for www, and an MX record. Verify that toString() contains each of these lines (in the typical master‑file order: $ORIGIN, $TTL, SOA, NS, MX, A).

group: Zone with Mandatory SOA and NS

cases.expected: String that starts with the SOA line followed by at least one NS line – toString() must always include the zone’s SOA and NS records when they exist.
cases.description: Add only a SOA and an NS record to a new Zone. Ensure that the string returned by toString() begins with the SOA record line and contains the NS record line.

cases.expected: String that no longer contains the removed TXT record – toString() reflects the current state of the zone.
cases.description: Add a TXT record to a Zone, then remove it using removeRecord(). Verify that toString() no longer includes the TXT line.

cases.expected: String that contains both duplicate A records (identical name/type but different data) – toString() must list each distinct RRset entry.
cases.description: Add two A records for the same name (www.example.com.) with different IP addresses. Verify that toString() includes both IP addresses on separate lines (or as a space‑separated list) for that name.

cases.expected: String whose length grows proportionally with the number of added records and contains all of them – toString() must handle many records without truncation or error.
cases.description: Add 1000 A records (host0.example.com., host1.example.com., …) to a Zone. Verify that toString() returns a string that contains the first and last host lines and that the total number of newline characters equals the number of records added plus the SOA/NS lines.

cases.expected: Exact equality between the results of toString() and toMasterFile() – the two methods must be interchangeable.
cases.description: For any Zone configuration (e.g., after adding a mix of records), assert that zone.toString().equals(zone.toMasterFile()).

Create a Zone instance and, using reflection, set its internal origin field to null. Invoking toString() should throw a NullPointerException because the method attempts to format the $ORIGIN directive using a null Name.

After constructing a Zone, force the internal map that stores RRsets (e.g., the TreeMap used by the zone) to null via reflection. Calling toString() will try to iterate over the map and raise a NullPointerException.

group: Add Null Record Leads to Exception

cases.description: Invoke zone.addRecord(null). The zone stores a null entry in its data structures. When toString() later iterates over the stored records it encounters the null and throws a NullPointerException.

Create a Record (or subclass) whose name field is null and add it to the zone via addRecord(). The zone validates arguments on insertion, but the validation is deferred until toString() formats the record, causing an IllegalArgumentException.
Create a Zone, add an NS record but do NOT add an SOA record. The toMasterFile() implementation expects at least one SOA and throws IllegalStateException when it cannot find one.

Add a Record whose toString() implementation throws an IOException (simulated via a custom Record subclass). When toString() builds the master‑file string, the IOException is caught and re‑thrown as a RuntimeException. The test expects that RuntimeException.

Start a thread that continuously adds records to a Zone while the main test thread calls zone.toString(). Because toMasterFile() iterates over the internal collection without making a defensive copy, a ConcurrentModificationException may be thrown.
